newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong, South Korea sign repo pact.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong, South Korea sign repo pact.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the territory's de facto central bank, said on Monday it had signed a bilateral repurchase (repo) agreement with the Bank of Korea, South Korea's central bank.
The pact is the HKMA's ninth repo agreement, it said in a statement.
The HKMA has bilateral repo agreements with the central banks of Australia, China, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand.
A bilateral repo agreement is a simultaneous agreement to buy securities for an agreed amount of cash and to sell back the same securities at a specific date for a specified amount.
Highly liquid U.S. dollar government securities are the instruments used in all of the repo agreements signed between the HKMA and regional central banks.
Repo agreements between central banks, whose credit standing is generally higher than those of private sector banks, would improve the central banks' liquidity under minimal risk, the HKMA said.
